issue: In assessing an entrapment defense, is the government's inducement tested objectively, by how a reasonable, law-abiding person would respond, or subjectively, by the particular defendant's predisposition and susceptibility?
provision: Entrapment defense (judicially created doctrine; no statute)

sides.position: The inducement test for entrapment is objective, focusing on the government's conduct in relation to a hypothetical reasonable, law-abiding citizen.
cases: United States v. Sanchez, 88 F.3d 1243 (D.C. Cir. 1996)

sides.position: The inducement test for entrapment is subjective, so the court may consider the defendant's particular characteristics and susceptibility to inducement.
cases: United States v. Williams, 547 F.3d 1187 (9th Cir. 2008)

quote: We not only have a circuit split but also lack any briefing on the objectivity or subjectivity of the test.
cite: United States v. Spradley, No. 23-3222 (10th Cir. 2025)
